about.tool: A broad-edged pen held at about 45°.
about.proportions: x-height about 5 nib widths; ascenders 1.4 x-heights (b and d higher, curving back); descenders about 0.4; capitals about 1.4.
about.features: Fraktur: round letters are 'bitten', a curved left side and a broken right side meeting in points (o, a, e, g, q); stems have diamond heads and feet cut to the right; the ascenders of b, h, k, l fork with a curved hairline at the top; f plunges below the line; capitals are built from the 'elephant trunk' (an S-shaped lobe under a heavy arch) with a heavy foot sweeping along the line. The exemplar has no figures; they are written in the same broken pen. Where the exemplar lifts the pen between a head, its stem and its foot, they are written here in one movement.
about.history: The German blackletter of the 16th century (the Theuerdank and the writing masters Johann Neudörffer and Wolfgang Fugger), used in German print until the 20th century.
